en: be very similar; look just like

examples.en: The two people's voices are really alike.
This painting looked just like the real one.
The son walks with a gait very like his father's.

examples.ko: 그 사건은 작년에 일어난 일과 흡사할 거예요.
examples.en: That incident is probably much like what happened last year.
The dream was so close to reality that it was scary.

examples.ko: 쌍둥이처럼 흡사하게 생긴 두 가게가 나란히 있어요.
examples.en: Two shops that look as alike as twins stand side by side.

explain: '비슷하다'보다 딱딱하고 '거의 같다'에 가까워요. 보통 '~와 흡사하다'로 쓰고, 일상 대화에서는 '닮았다', '비슷하다'를 더 많이 써요.
explain_en: This is a stiffer, more written word than '비슷하다' and leans toward 'almost identical'. It is usually used as '~와 흡사하다'; in everyday speech people more often say '닮았다' or '비슷하다'.

en: despise; look down on with contempt

examples.en: He despises people who lie.

examples.ko: 저는 약한 사람을 괴롭히는 사람을 경멸했어요.
examples.en: I looked down on people who bully the weak.

examples.ko: 사람들이 그를 경멸할 만한 이유가 있어요.
examples.en: There is a reason people might look down on him.
A tone that shows contempt for others is uncomfortable to hear.

examples.ko: 그녀는 돈만 아는 상사를 경멸하고 멀리했어요.
examples.en: She held her money-obsessed boss in contempt and kept her distance.

examples.ko: 누구도 경멸해서는 안 된다고 어머니가 말씀하셨어요.
examples.en: My mother said we must never look down on anyone.

explain: '무시하다'는 신경 쓰지 않는 것이고, '경멸하다'는 상대를 아주 낮게 보고 싫어하는 것이에요. 감정이 훨씬 강해서 일상 대화보다 글이나 뉴스에서 더 자주 나와요.
explain_en: '무시하다' means to ignore or pay no attention, while '경멸하다' means to look down on someone and dislike them intensely. The feeling is much stronger, and it appears more in writing and news than in daily conversation.

examples.ko: 밤사이 도시에 공습이 있었다는 뉴스가 나왔어요.
examples.en: The news said there was an air raid on the city overnight.

examples.ko: 공습 경보가 울리자 사람들이 지하로 내려갔어요.
examples.en: When the air raid siren sounded, people went underground.

examples.ko: 할머니는 전쟁 때 공습을 피해 시골로 갔어요.
examples.en: My grandmother fled to the countryside to escape air raids during the war.
They rebuilt the building that collapsed in the air raid.

examples.ko: 박물관에서 공습 때 쓰던 대피소를 봤어요.
examples.en: At the museum I saw a shelter that was used during air raids.

examples.ko: 그 영화는 공습 장면이 아주 길어요.
examples.en: That movie has a very long bombing-raid scene.

explain: '공격'은 모든 종류의 공격이고, '공습'은 비행기나 미사일로 하늘에서 하는 공격을 가리켜요. 전쟁 뉴스에서 '공습 경보', '공습을 받다'처럼 자주 나와요. 불시에 치는 '기습'과는 달라요.
explain_en: '공격' covers any kind of attack, while '공습' refers to an attack from the air by planes or missiles. It shows up in war news as '공습 경보' (air raid siren) or '공습을 받다' (to come under air attack). It is different from '기습', a surprise attack of any kind.

examples.en: The police are quietly investigating that company.

examples.ko: 검찰은 그 사건을 몇 달째 내사해 왔어요.
examples.en: Prosecutors have been looking into that case quietly for months.
After receiving the report, the police began a preliminary investigation right away.

examples.ko: 정식 수사 전에 먼저 내사할 거예요.
examples.en: They will do a preliminary investigation before the formal one.

examples.ko: 내사하는 중이라서 자세한 내용은 알려 줄 수 없어요.
examples.en: Because it is still under preliminary investigation, details can't be shared.

examples.ko: 의혹이 사실인지 내사해야 한다고 기자가 말했어요.
examples.en: The reporter said they must look into whether the allegation is true.

explain: '수사하다'는 정식으로 사건을 조사하는 것이고, '내사하다'는 정식 수사를 시작하기 전에 조용히 알아보는 단계예요. 주로 경찰·검찰 뉴스에서 나오고 일상 대화에서는 거의 안 써요.
explain_en: '수사하다' is a formal criminal investigation, while '내사하다' is the quiet fact-finding stage before a formal case opens. You will mostly see it in police and prosecutor news, almost never in daily talk.

en: listless; lethargic; lacking energy and drive

examples.en: These days I don't want to do anything and I feel drained.
On rainy days my body felt listless.

examples.ko: 무기력한 하루가 계속되면 산책을 해 보세요.
examples.en: If listless days keep dragging on, try taking a walk.
After failing the exam, I lost all my drive.
He sat there limply and just looked out the window.

examples.ko: 회사에서 매일 같은 일을 하니까 무기력해서 쉬고 싶어요.
examples.en: Doing the same thing every day at work leaves me listless, and I want a break.

explain: '피곤하다'는 몸이 지친 것이고, '무기력하다'는 마음에 힘이 없어서 아무것도 하고 싶지 않은 상태예요. '우울하다'와 같이 쓰일 때도 많지만, 슬픔보다 '힘이 없음'에 가까워요.
explain_en: '피곤하다' is about a tired body, while '무기력하다' is when your spirit has no energy and you don't feel like doing anything. It often goes along with '우울하다', but it is closer to 'no energy' than to sadness.

en: be found out; be revealed; come to light (something hidden)

examples.en: What I did in secret was found out in the end.
The thief in hiding gets discovered by the police.
If cheating on an exam is discovered, you are in big trouble.
I was worried the secret would come to light.
Only after being found out did he tell the truth.
I tried not to get caught, but it ended up being discovered.

explain: '들키다'는 일상에서 누구에게나 쓰고, '발각되다'는 나쁜 일이나 비밀이 드러났을 때 뉴스나 글에서 더 많이 써요. 친구나 가족에게 걸렸을 때는 '들켰어요'가 자연스러워요.
explain_en: '들키다' is the everyday word for getting caught, while '발각되다' is used more in news and writing when something bad or secret comes out. When your friend or family catches you, '들켰어요' sounds more natural.

examples.en: In the movie, the sheriff protects the town.

examples.ko: 보안관은 가슴에 별 모양 배지를 달고 있어요.
examples.en: The sheriff wears a star-shaped badge on his chest.
I like the sheriffs in Western movies.

examples.ko: 마을 사람들은 새 보안관에게 도움을 청했어요.
examples.en: The townspeople asked the new sheriff for help.
The kids run around playing sheriff.

examples.ko: 그 소년은 보안관과 함께 도둑을 잡았어요.
examples.en: The boy caught the thief together with the sheriff.

explain: 보안관은 주로 서부 영화나 미국 이야기에서 들을 수 있는 말이에요. 한국에서 비슷한 일을 하는 사람은 '경찰관'이지만, 보안관은 한 지역을 지키는 이미지가 강해요.
explain_en: '보안관' is a word you mostly hear in Western movies or stories about the US. The closest Korean role is '경찰관', but '보안관' has a strong image of guarding one local area.

en: flatter to win favor; suck up

examples.en: He got promoted by sucking up to the boss.
People who flatter you for favors are hard to trust.

examples.ko: 아부할 줄 몰라서 손해를 볼 때가 있어요.
examples.en: I don't know how to butter people up, so I sometimes lose out.
I flattered the teacher to get a good grade.
Please don't flatter me and just be honest.
If you flatter people like that, they trust you less.

explain: '칭찬하다'는 진심일 수 있지만 '아부하다'는 잘 보이려고 하는 말과 행동이라 늘 부정적이에요. '아첨하다'도 비슷하고, '비위를 맞추다'는 조금 더 가벼운 표현이에요.
explain_en: '칭찬하다' can be sincere, but '아부하다' means words and actions meant to win favor, so it is always negative. '아첨하다' is similar, and '비위를 맞추다' is a slightly lighter expression.

examples.en: The airport has so many passengers that the lines are long.

examples.ko: 이 배는 여객과 화물을 같이 실어요.
examples.en: This ship carries both passengers and cargo.
I went to Jeju Island on a passenger ferry.
The passenger terminal is in the city center.
The number of passengers rose compared with last year.
The passenger plane arrived later than scheduled.

explain: '승객'은 버스·택시·지하철까지 탄 사람을 두루 가리키는 일상어고, '여객'은 여객선·여객기·여객 터미널처럼 교통 사업이나 공항·항만 뉴스에서 쓰는 딱딱한 말이에요. 말할 때는 '승객'이 훨씬 자연스러워요.
explain_en: '승객' is the everyday word for anyone riding a bus, taxi, or subway, while '여객' is a stiffer word used in transport business and airport or port news, as in '여객선', '여객기', '여객 터미널'. In speech, '승객' sounds much more natural.

en: precarious; perilous; critical; on the verge of collapse

examples.en: The bridge is old, so it is precarious to cross.
That company is in a precarious situation right now.

examples.ko: 아이가 높은 난간에 위태하게 서 있었어요.
examples.en: The child was standing precariously on the high railing.
My health was in danger, so I was admitted to the hospital.
The patient whose life had been in danger woke up.

examples.ko: 경기가 나빠져서 가게가 위태할 것 같아요.
examples.en: The economy got worse, so the shop looks like it is in danger.

explain: '위험하다'는 다치거나 문제가 생길 가능성이 있다는 뜻이고, '위태하다'는 곧 무너질 것처럼 아슬아슬한 상태에 써요. 말할 때는 '위태롭다'가 더 흔하고 뜻은 거의 같아요.
explain_en: '위험하다' says something could cause harm, while '위태하다' describes a shaky, about-to-collapse state. In speech '위태롭다' is more common and means almost the same.

examples.en: The criminal confessed everything at the police station.
If you confess your wrongdoing, your mind feels at ease.
He admitted his lie and apologized.
Some people never confess to the end.
The child confesses to having broken the window.
I didn't have the courage to confess, so I kept hiding it.

explain: '고백하다'는 사랑이나 비밀 같은 마음을 말할 때도 쓰지만, '자백하다'는 자기가 한 나쁜 일이나 죄만 말할 때 써요. 가벼운 잘못에는 '털어놓다'나 '실토하다'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: '고백하다' can be used for love or secrets, but '자백하다' is only for admitting your own wrongdoing or crime. For minor faults, '털어놓다' or '실토하다' sounds more natural.

examples.ko: 이 지역에서는 석탄 채굴이 오래전에 끝났어요.
examples.en: Coal mining in this area ended long ago.
It is a town that was famous for gold mining.
Bitcoin mining uses a lot of electricity.
I met people who work at a mining site.

examples.ko: 바다 밑에서 하는 채굴은 환경에 영향을 줘요.
examples.en: Mining on the seabed affects the environment.
The government did not permit the mining.

explain: '캐다'는 감자·약초·광석을 땅에서 파내는 일상 동사고, '채굴'은 광산·자원 개발 뉴스에서 쓰는 명사예요. 요즘은 '비트코인 채굴'처럼 컴퓨터로 가상화폐를 얻는 일에도 써요.
explain_en: '캐다' is an everyday verb for digging potatoes, herbs, or ore out of the ground, while '채굴' is a noun used in mining and resource-development news. Today it is also used for '비트코인 채굴', getting cryptocurrency with computers.

en: capital contribution; putting money into a business

examples.en: The investment needed for the new business has grown.
The government promised to put money into the research institute.
The more you put in, the bigger your share gets.

examples.ko: 두 회사의 공동 출자로 공장이 세워졌어요.
examples.en: The factory was built through a joint investment by the two companies.

examples.ko: 출자에는 위험이 따르니까 잘 생각해야 해요.
examples.en: Putting in money carries risk, so think carefully.

examples.ko: 형의 출자 덕분에 가게를 열 수 있었어요.
examples.en: Thanks to my older brother's investment, I could open the shop.

explain: '투자'는 이익을 바라고 돈을 넣는 넓은 말이고, '출자'는 회사를 세우거나 사업에 참여하려고 돈이나 물건을 내는 쪽에 가까워요. 뉴스와 경제 글에서 '출자금', '공동 출자'로 자주 나와요.
explain_en: '투자' is the broad word for putting money in hoping for profit, while '출자' leans toward contributing money or assets to found a company or take part in a business. In news and finance writing you often see '출자금' and '공동 출자'.

examples.en: The neighboring country's army crossed the border.
You must not invade other people's privacy.

examples.ko: 동생이 제 방을 침범해서 화가 났어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling barged into my room, and I got angry.

examples.ko: 새로 온 사람이 제 자리를 침범하는 것 같아요.
examples.en: It feels like the newcomer is encroaching on my spot.
Do not infringe on other people's rights.
I demanded an apology from the person who had intruded.

explain: '침입하다'는 건물이나 장소에 몰래 들어가는 쪽이고, '침범하다'는 땅·권리·사생활 같은 남의 영역을 넘어오는 쪽이에요. 도둑은 '침입'하고, 영해와 사생활은 '침범'해요.
explain_en: '침입하다' is about sneaking into a building or place, while '침범하다' is about crossing into someone else's territory, rights, or privacy. A thief '침입하다', but territorial waters and privacy are '침범하다'.

examples.en: Residents were shocked by the news of the school mergers and closures.
The district office is reviewing merging and cutting departments.

examples.ko: 인구가 줄면서 작은 학교의 통폐합이 이어져요.
examples.en: As the population shrinks, small schools keep being merged or closed.
The restructuring changed the staff's work a lot.
Opinions are divided on merging and closing public agencies.

examples.ko: 통폐합은 비용을 줄이려고 하지만 불편도 생겨요.
examples.en: Mergers and closures aim to cut costs, but they cause inconvenience too.

explain: '통합'은 하나로 합치는 것, '폐지'는 없애는 것인데, '통폐합'은 이 둘을 묶은 말로 학교·기관·부서를 줄이거나 합칠 때 써요. 주로 뉴스나 행정 글에서 나와요.
explain_en: '통합' means joining into one and '폐지' means abolishing; '통폐합' bundles both and is used when schools, agencies, or departments are merged or cut. It appears mainly in news and administrative writing.

examples.en: The retainer said to the emperor, 'Your Majesty, I beg to report.'

examples.ko: 사극에서 폐하라고 부르는 장면을 많이 봐요.
examples.en: I often see scenes in period dramas where they call the emperor 'Your Majesty'.
The retainer announced that His Majesty the Emperor had arrived.
The general set out after receiving the Emperor's order.

examples.ko: 영화 속 왕비는 폐하를 몹시 걱정했어요.
examples.en: In the movie, the queen worried about the Emperor deeply.

examples.ko: 폐하 앞에서는 고개를 들 수 없었어요.
examples.en: In front of the Emperor, no one could lift their head.

explain: 역사극에서 황제에게는 '폐하', 조선의 왕에게는 '전하'라고 불러요. 지금은 사극이나 외국 왕실 이야기에서만 들을 수 있어요.
explain_en: In historical dramas an emperor is addressed as '폐하', while a Joseon king is addressed as '전하'. Today you hear it only in period dramas or stories about foreign royal families.

examples.en: The government officially announced the new policy.

examples.ko: 시험 결과는 다음 주에 공표할 거예요.
examples.en: The exam results will be made public next week.

examples.ko: 회사는 계획을 공표하기 전에 직원에게 먼저 알렸어요.
examples.en: The company told employees first before announcing the plan publicly.
You must keep it secret until the day it is announced.

examples.ko: 연구 결과를 공표하면 사람들이 관심을 가져요.
examples.en: When research results are made public, people take an interest.

examples.ko: 선거 결과를 공표해서 모두 알게 되었어요.
examples.en: They announced the election results, so everyone found out.

explain: '발표하다'는 학교에서 과제를 말할 때도 쓰지만, '공표하다'는 정부·기관이 법이나 결과를 공식적으로 세상에 알릴 때만 써요. 일상 대화에서는 거의 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: '발표하다' can be used even for presenting homework at school, but '공표하다' is only for a government or institution officially announcing laws or results to the public. It is rarely used in everyday talk.

examples.en: I toughen up my body by running every day.
He trained his mind from a young age.
Swimming is good for building up your body.
I signed up at the gym to build my stamina.

examples.ko: 선수들은 겨울 동안 더 열심히 단련할 거예요.
examples.en: The players will train even harder during the winter.

examples.ko: 매일 단련하면 어려운 동작도 할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you train every day, you can do difficult moves too.

explain: '운동하다'는 몸을 움직이는 일반적인 말이고, '단련하다'는 몸이나 마음을 반복해서 강하게 만든다는 느낌이 있어요. '몸을 단련하다', '정신을 단련하다'처럼 목적어는 주로 몸·마음·기술이에요.
explain_en: '운동하다' is the general word for exercising, while '단련하다' carries the sense of repeatedly making your body or mind stronger. Its objects are mostly body, mind, or skill, as in '몸을 단련하다' and '정신을 단련하다'.

en: be tight against; stick tightly; be in close contact

examples.en: The baby fell asleep nestled tightly against its mother.
A mask only works if it fits tightly against the face.

examples.ko: 두 부품이 밀착되지 않아서 물이 새요.
examples.en: The two parts don't fit tightly together, so water leaks.
They say we need policies that stay close to residents.
I bought a sports outfit that hugs the body.
Because of the humidity, the paper stuck flat to the wall.

explain: '붙다'는 가장 흔한 말이고, '밀착되다'는 틈 없이 딱 붙어 있는 상태를 강조해요. 몸·옷·부품뿐 아니라 '현장에 밀착된 정책'처럼 비유로도 써요.
explain_en: '붙다' is the most common word, while '밀착되다' stresses sticking with no gap at all. It is used for bodies, clothes, and parts, and also figuratively, as in '현장에 밀착된 정책' (a policy close to the field).
